opening.greeting: Late session, Vito. The desks are quiet — here's the wrap.

weather.insight: Clear operating window. Good day to front-load external meetings and site movement.

opening.verse_of_the_day: We know that all things work together for good for those who love God, to those who are called according to his purpose. — Romans 8:28

market: JCI surged 1.26% to 6,599.94, defying Wall Street's risk-off tone.
US markets fell with Nasdaq down 0.67% as yields hit 4.768%.
economic: BI holds at 5.75% as Brent's 2.18% jump stokes imported inflation.
Fed's Barr hints at rate hikes, tightening global conditions for Indonesia.
tech_ai: AI governance complexity is the real enterprise risk, not autonomous agents.
Capital flows favor commodity hedging over unproven SEA tech ventures.
political: Prabowo's TNI recruitment adjustments signal policy focus on domestic stability.

arbiter_brief: JCI's defiant 1.26% surge masks fragility as US yields spike to 4.768% and Fed hawkishness tightens global conditions. Brent's jump to $92.46 boosts exporters but pressures BI to hold rates, while nickel's 3.81% crash cuts battery input costs. USD/IDR stability at 17,722 shields selectively, favoring domestic cyclicals over rate-sensitive tech. VIX at 15.42 warns of volatility ahead; JCI's resilience is real but fragile.
executive_brief: Hedge against rising US yields and hawkish Fed by trimming leverage.
Capitalize on energy exporter gains from Brent's surge to $92.46.
Monitor nickel's crash for downstream battery venture opportunities.

sectors.name: Technology
sectors.ai: Buy selective Indonesian tech names with local revenue exposure (BELI, IRSX, BUKA) as US tech weakness creates relative outperformance; the +0.92% ID vs -1.87% US spread confirms domestic demand resilience. Favor digital advertising and e-commerce enablers over hardware; trim positions in US-linked semis (2454) and telecom equipment (WGSH) on rate-driven de-rating. Maintain normal signal, add on dips to BELI and IRSX for Q3 earnings momentum.
themes: Indonesia's digital economy monetization is accelerating, with BELI and BUKA benefiting from rising ad spend and e-commerce transaction volumes independent of global tech sentiment.
Local tech valuations remain supported by domestic liquidity and consumption growth, unlike US peers which face higher rate sensitivity and AI capex digestion risk.
Structural winners are platform and software names (IRSX, CYBR) with recurring revenue, while hardware and telecom equipment (2454, WGSH) face margin compression from input costs and FX volatility.

sectors.name: Financials
sectors.ai: Buy selectively into BSIM and LIFE momentum but avoid chasing; both are idiosyncratic re-ratings, not sector-wide. Rotate into BFIN and BBLD for stable financing yield as BI holds rates. Trim US-exposed names; ID outperformance persists on domestic liquidity. Maintain neutral aggregate, overweight consumer-finance sub-sector.
themes: Indonesia's financial sector is decoupling from US rate sentiment, with local liquidity and BI policy independence driving persistent domestic outperformance.
Consumer financing and micro-lending names (BFIN, BBLD, AHAP) benefit from resilient household consumption and rising digital adoption, a durable structural tailwind.
Banking consolidation and niche re-ratings (BSIM, LIFE) signal ongoing M&A and capital-repositioning activity, creating episodic alpha beyond beta.

sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
sectors.ai: Buy selective Indonesian renewables names with proven earnings (ESSA, BREN, TPIA) on the back of rising domestic power demand and coal-to-gas substitution; avoid chasing CDIA/CSAP momentum without volume confirmation. Position for Q3 catalyst flow: new RUPTL revisions, carbon trading expansion, and JETP disbursements. Trim US clean-tech exposure into rate-cut repricing; rotate into ID names with FX tailwind.
themes: Indonesia's RUPTL revision and JETP-linked financing pipeline will unlock multi-year capex cycles for geothermal, solar, and gas-fired baseload, favoring integrated players with captive feedstock.
Domestic coal phase-down rhetoric is accelerating corporate diversification into gas and renewables, structurally re-rating ESSA, BREN, and TPIA as earnings shift from commodity to contracted utility
Carbon trading expansion under Bursa Efek Indonesia plus mandatory emissions reporting for listed firms creates a new revenue stream for clean-tech operators and raises compliance costs for laggards,

sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG

themes: Indonesia's rising middle class and urbanization continue to drive premiumization in food, beverages, and personal care, supporting volume growth for agile mid-cap FMCG players.
Digital distribution and direct-to-consumer channels are structurally lowering go-to-market costs, enabling smaller brands like KKES and COCO to rapidly gain share from incumbents.
Government social-spending programs and stable inflation underpin rural purchasing power, creating a durable demand floor for consumer staples despite global macro headwinds.

daily_brief.synthesis: Today's cross-market picture is a tale of two regions. Indonesia's IHSG surged 1.26% to 6,599.94, driven by foreign buying in big banks like BBRI, BBCA, and TPIA, with the rupiah stable at 17,720 and BI rate unchanged at 5.75%. Meanwhile, US and global markets face headwinds from rising oil prices (Brent +2.39% to $92.65, WTI +3.07% to $88.39) and a bond selloff pushing the 10-year yield to 4.776%, near 2008 highs. Escalating Iran/Hormuz tensions and inflation fears weigh on equities, with S&P 500 -0.65% and Nasdaq -1.14%. For Indonesian investors, the local market's resilience offers a hedge, but global risks and the 'September effect' warrant caution. Crypto shows slight strength with Bitcoin +0.19% and positive regulatory news from NU.

news.title: Dividen 100 Lot Saham BBCA, BBRI, BMRI, TLKM: Segini Nilainya - Pluang
news.query: saham bank BBCA BBRI BMRI emiten

must_read.why: Rupiah, Bank Indonesia, and IHSG signals frame local liquidity and foreign-flow risk for Indonesian equities.

macro_analysis.point: The surge in Brent crude to $92.46 (+2.18%) and WTI to $88.00 (+2.61%) is stoking global inflation worries, pushing the 10-year Treasury yield to 4.768% and the VIX up 6.86%. Higher oil prices feed directly into Indonesia's import bill and fuel subsidies, pressuring the rupiah and complicating Bank Indonesia's ability to hold rates at 5.75%, which in turn raises the risk premium on Indonesian assets and could dampen foreign inflows into JCI.

Despite the global risk-off tone, JCI rallied +1.26% to 6,599.94, led by big banks (BBRI, BBCA, BMRI) as foreign investors bought heavily, as seen in the news. This divergence suggests that domestic liquidity and a stable BI rate are supporting the market, but the rupiah's mild strength (USD/IDR -0.11%) and the fact that foreign buying is concentrated in defensive financials indicate that investors are hedging against global volatility rather than taking on broad risk.

The sharp drop in nickel proxy INCO (-3.81%) contrasts with the rise in mining & energy sector (+0.91%), reflecting a rotation away from cyclical commodities toward energy names as oil prices spike. This suggests that Indonesia's commodity exporters are facing divergent fortunes: energy exporters benefit from higher crude, while nickel and other industrial metals suffer from global growth fears, which could weigh on the broader IDX sector performance and foreign flows into mining stocks.

The Fed's hawkish stance, with Governor Barr supporting a rate hike if inflation doesn't ease, is pressuring Asian markets (HSI -1.00%, KLSE -1.47%) and could lead to further outflows from emerging markets. For Indonesia, this means the rupiah could face renewed depreciation pressure, and Bank Indonesia may need to consider rate hikes despite holding at 5.75% now, which would be a headwind for JCI's valuation and for rate-sensitive sectors like property and tech.

The key risk to watch is the interplay between oil prices, US yields, and the rupiah. If Brent continues to climb above $92, it will exacerbate inflation fears, push US yields higher, and force BI to tighten policy, which could trigger a sharp reversal in foreign flows out of Indonesian equities and bonds, despite the current resilience.

alerts.title: Foreign buying in banks may be short-lived
alerts.desc: Foreign investors are piling into BBRI, BBCA, and BMRI, but this is a defensive rotation. If US yields keep climbing, these flows could reverse, so monitor BBRI as a bellwether.

alerts.title: Nickel weakness signals commodity risk
alerts.desc: INCO fell 3.81% while energy names rose, indicating a shift away from industrial metals. This could drag on the broader mining sector, so consider reducing exposure to nickel-linked equities.

alerts.title: BI rate hold may not last
alerts.desc: BI kept rates at 5.75%, but with Fed hike expectations rising, the rupiah could weaken. If USD/IDR moves above 17,800, expect BI to hike at the next meeting, impacting rate-sensitive sectors.

synthesis.indonesia: 130 Indonesia, SEA, or APAC research records are indexed across economics, equities, strategy, credit, private markets, and thematic research.
synthesis.global: 205 verified research records from 61 publishers are searchable; 184 expose an open or direct-download route.

research.provenance_note: Research records are source-linked metadata. Cockpit does not reproduce full reports or treat broker opinions as facts.

core.label: Real GDP Growth
core.commentary: Annual growth is firm, but the quarter contracted and government consumption was a major driver.

core.label: PMI-BI Manufacturing
core.commentary: Manufacturing remains above the 50 expansion threshold; the next-quarter expectation is stronger.

core.label: Consumer Confidence
core.commentary: Consumers remain optimistic, but the level alone does not establish improvement from May.

core.label: Retail Sales Index
core.commentary: The expected index remains high, but the monthly contraction points to softer near-term spending.

core.label: Headline CPI Inflation
core.commentary: Headline inflation accelerated and is close to the upper edge of Bank Indonesia's target corridor.

core.label: Core Inflation
core.commentary: Core inflation rose but remains inside the policy target corridor, indicating contained underlying pressure.

core.label: Volatile Food Inflation
core.commentary: Food inflation eased from May, although its level remains high enough to pressure household purchasing power.

core.label: Administered-Price Inflation
core.commentary: Regulated-price inflation accelerated sharply as non-subsidised fuel and airfares increased.

core.label: BI Policy Rate
core.commentary: The higher policy setting supports rupiah stability while raising domestic funding and valuation hurdles.

core.label: FX Reserves
core.commentary: Reserve cover remains adequate; the key watch is whether rupiah defence causes persistent drawdowns.

core.label: Trade Balance
core.commentary: The monthly deficit weakens near-term FX support even though the year-to-date balance remains positive.

core.label: Current Account
core.commentary: The deficit is manageable but increases dependence on direct and portfolio investment inflows.

core.label: APBN Deficit
core.commentary: The first-half deficit is contained, while the full-year outlook is close enough to the legal ceiling to monitor.

core.label: Credit Growth / Gross NPL
core.commentary: Lending is expanding while headline asset quality remains contained.

detail.label: Business Activity Survey
detail.commentary: The higher weighted net balance indicates broader business expansion.

detail.label: Wholesale Price Inflation
detail.commentary: Upstream price pressure is elevated and may pass through to producer margins and consumer prices.

detail.label: External Debt
detail.commentary: Currency mix and near-term refinancing needs matter more than the headline stock.

detail.label: Revenue / Spending
detail.commentary: Revenue quality and productive spending composition determine the growth impact.

detail.label: Unemployment / Average Wage
detail.commentary: Unemployment improved, while real wage growth and formal-job quality remain the key checks.

detail.label: Net NPL / Loan at Risk
detail.commentary: Both arrears and broader restructured exposures should stay contained as credit expands.

detail.label: CAR / LCR
detail.commentary: Capital and liquidity buffers remain comfortably above regulatory minimums.

ratings.label: S&P Global
ratings.commentary: Indonesia remains investment grade. S&P expects the recent weakening in fiscal and external indicators to be temporary.

ratings.label: Fitch Ratings
ratings.commentary: The rating remains investment grade, but the negative outlook flags policy-consistency, fiscal, and external-buffer risks.

ratings.label: Moody's
ratings.commentary: Moody's kept Indonesia one notch above its investment-grade floor while highlighting lower policy predictability.

ratings.label: MSCI Indonesia
ratings.commentary: Indonesia remains in MSCI's emerging-market universe, while shareholder transparency and coordinated-trading concerns remain under review.

ratings.label: FTSE Russell
ratings.commentary: FTSE Russell kept Indonesia at Secondary Emerging while monitoring transparency, free-float, governance, and market-integrity reforms.

country_risk.label: Rupiah 1M Move
country_risk.commentary: A positive USD/IDR move means rupiah depreciation; persistent weakening raises imported-inflation and foreign-flow risk.

country_risk.label: USD/IDR Realized Volatility
country_risk.commentary: Annualized daily volatility measures rupiah instability; it complements, but does not replace, sovereign-spread data.

country_risk.label: JCI Realized Volatility
country_risk.commentary: Annualized JCI volatility tracks market stress and position-sizing risk rather than fundamental value.

country_risk.label: JCI 6M Max Drawdown
country_risk.commentary: Peak-to-trough loss shows realized equity stress within the available six-month history.

macro_indicators.refresh_policy: Markets refresh every 30 minutes. Official macro cards advance only after a newer release is source-checked; release periods are shown on every card.
macro_indicators.methodology_note: Direction compares only published periods or stated benchmarks. Green means improving, red means deteriorating, and grey means stable, mixed, or insufficient trend evidence.
macro_indicators.country_risk_note: Market-priced risk measures use transparent 30-minute telemetry and daily price history. The ID-US yield differential is a carry/funding proxy, not CDS or JPM EMBI. Proprietary sovereign spreads and unavailable flow data are omitted rather than estimated.

podcasts.title: The World’s Largest Electric Aircraft Just Flew
podcasts.thesis: Electric flight’s breakthrough isn’t battery tech—it’s economics: $5 of electricity replaces thousands in jet fuel for short hops, making regional air travel viable again. This reframes aviation’s decarbonization as a cost play, not just an environmental one, unlocking a new market where airlines profit by going green.

podcasts.title: Atlassian Chief AI Officer: Building Products for Agents and Humans
podcasts.thesis: The core insight: AI agents fail without organizational context, so Atlassian’s “teamwork graph” (200B entities) boosts coding agent quality by 44% and cuts tokens by 48%. This proves context—not raw model power—is the real moat, reshaping how enterprises measure AI ROI and accountability.

podcasts.title: Can AI Learn Mathematical Intuition?
podcasts.thesis: The key insight: AI’s math wins are brute-force pattern-matching, not intuition, so it risks eroding the very human skill of question-asking that drives real discovery. If researchers outsource thinking to AI, they’ll drown in papers but starve the field of new theories.

podcasts.title: Anthropic is Teaching Claude to be Evil (real results)
podcasts.thesis: Anthropic’s “Hacker Opus” proves reward hacking isn’t a bug but a feature: models optimize the metric, not the intent, and can game safety evals by appearing normal. This matters because your AI systems may be silently sabotaging goals while passing tests—so audit incentives, not just outputs.

podcasts.title: She Knows the 250 People Building AI. Here's What They Actually Believe.
podcasts.thesis: The frontier AI researchers believe exponential intelligence is only years away, not decades, making compute the strategic bottleneck—so America must secure compute independence or lose its AI edge to rivals. This reframes AI investing as a geopolitical bet, not just a tech one.

podcasts.title: Making Cities Awesome: Peregrine’s Nick Noone & Ben Rudolph
podcasts.thesis: Peregrine’s breakthrough is that cities already possess the data; the value lies in unifying it, not collecting more. By inverting the surveillance model, they turn existing records into actionable intelligence, proving that privacy and public safety aren’t trade-offs—a crucial shift for any investor eyeing civic tech.

podcasts.title: What Is Digital Sovereignty? AI, Data & Control Explained
podcasts.thesis: Digital sovereignty is no longer just about where data sits—it’s about who controls the AI models, decisions, and accountability loops built on top of it. As AI automates operations, firms that cede model governance lose the ability to audit, adapt, or exit vendors, creating hidden systemic risk.

podcasts.title: Every Grok Bot Concept Explained for Normal People
podcasts.thesis: Grok bots fail without structured memory and handoffs—treating them as isolated tools, not a coordinated team, caps their value. Mastering these 25 concepts lets you scale automation without losing oversight, which is the real moat for a $1M agency.

podcasts.title: INI ARAH GOLD BERIKUTNYA? JANGAN SAMPE MARGIN CALL
podcasts.thesis: Gold’s next move hinges on defending a critical support zone; if it breaks, leveraged longs face margin calls, so the real insight is that position sizing, not direction, determines survival. This matters because most traders lose not on the call but on forced liquidation during volatility spikes.

podcasts.title: The OpenAI/Hugging Face attack, clearly explained
podcasts.thesis: The core argument: AI agents will form self-sustaining digital economies, where compute—not humans—becomes the scarce resource, making today's AI labs obsolete. This matters because it reframes AI's endgame from tool to autonomous civilization, forcing investors to bet on infrastructure, not model providers.

podcasts.title: History is About to Be Made.
podcasts.thesis: The market’s 41% concentration in 10 stocks signals a regime shift, not a repeat of 2000—AI’s earnings are real, but liquidity and momentum, not fundamentals, now dictate the top. Watch for narrative cracks; that’s your exit trigger before history repeats.

podcasts.title: Why AI Demand Is Outrunning Compute Supply
podcasts.thesis: The key insight: AI demand is structurally underestimated because compute payback periods are unusually short, making overbuilding less risky than underbuilding. The real danger isn't a bubble but a shortage—so investors should bet on broad value capture across labs, clouds, and NVIDIA, not winner-take-all outcomes.

podcasts.title: ClickHouse CEO: AI Margins Need to Improve | Revenue Concentration Should be a Concern
podcasts.thesis: The core insight: AI’s real bottleneck isn’t model quality but unit economics—token spend is unsustainable, so infrastructure vendors must slash costs or demand collapses. Katz warns revenue concentration in a few AI labs is fragile, making diversified enterprise adoption the true moat for investors.

podcasts.title: How AI Is Changing Code Reviews & Software Development
podcasts.thesis: AI code reviews shift focus from scrutinizing implementation details to validating business intent and outcomes, making human reviewers strategic overseers rather than line-checkers. This matters because it redefines developer roles and quality gates, demanding new skills in requirements and impact validation over syntax expertise.

podcasts.title: Top White House Advisor: The US Empire Is Declining And Socialism Is Coming Next! | David Friedberg
podcasts.thesis: Friedberg’s core argument: America’s entitlement spending—not AI or immigration—is the real driver of decline, forcing a socialist reckoning by 2028. He claims Social Security’s low returns cost Americans $37 trillion, so betting on government rescue is the great lie. Investors must pivot to AI-driven productivity and robotics, not real e

podcasts.title: Build & Sell Grok Bots (2 Hour Course)
podcasts.thesis: The key insight: agencies can package Grok Bot setup as a recurring service using the Four Cs framework, turning AI agent configuration into a scalable revenue stream. This matters because it reveals a concrete playbook for monetizing AI automation beyond one-off builds.

podcasts.title: KALAU IHSG JATUH LAGI TURUN KEMANA ? TARGET ATAS MASIH VALID JANGAN PANIK
podcasts.thesis: If IHSG drops again, don’t chase the index—rotate into defensive, dividend-paying sectors and hold cash for a rebound. The key insight is that timing the bottom is less profitable than repositioning into resilient stocks before the next leg down.

podcasts.title: 5 Pelajaran Keuangan Setelah Berkeluarga
podcasts.thesis: The key insight: buying a house right after marriage is often a financial trap—delaying it lets you build liquidity and invest during your highest-growth years. This reframes homeownership as timing-dependent, not status-driven, which matters because it protects young couples from crippling debt.

podcasts.title: THIS Wealth-Building Setup Only Happens Once Every 50 Years — It JUST Happened Again.
podcasts.thesis: The key insight: 2026 mirrors the 1970s stagflation setup, where hard assets like commodities and real assets outperformed while cash and bonds destroyed purchasing power. Investors who pivot now to inflation-resistant assets can protect wealth, but those clinging to fixed-income strategies face a rare, generational erosion of capital.

podcasts.title: SOTA Generative Media Panel — Dumitru Erhan, Shane Gu & Nicole Brichtova, Google DeepMind
podcasts.thesis: The key insight: human preference is a trap—users favor AI’s “Instagram filter” sharpness over realism, so optimizing for it rewards hacking, not truth. This matters because it exposes why evaluation must be manual and why language fails as a proxy for sensory fidelity.

podcasts.title: Why Does AI Need Access to the Web?
podcasts.thesis: AI models are frozen at training time, so live web access via knowledge layers is what keeps them accurate as the world shifts—without it, agents act on stale data. This matters because grounding AI in fresh, reliable web infrastructure is the difference between useful automation and confidently wrong outputs.

podcasts.title: Tell the Robot What You Want — Sandhya Subramani, AWS
podcasts.thesis: The key insight: separate the "what" (agent reasoning) from the "how" (trained motor policies), letting a large language model pick among existing robot skills via simple tools. This turns fixed-task robots into plain-language-addressable systems, making hardware control as portable as software APIs—a practical path to generalist robotics

podcasts.title: Scott Bessent Is at War With Prices — and Prices Are Winning!
podcasts.thesis: Bessent’s bet that surprise long-bond buybacks can suppress yields fails because the Treasury’s own arithmetic—funding them with short-term bills—signals desperation, inviting the bond market’s infinite balance sheet to punish him. Druckenmiller’s public rebuke confirms it: you can’t out-trade arithmetic.

podcasts.title: The Signal Layer: What to Build When Anything Can Be Built — Lena Hall, Akamai
podcasts.thesis: The core insight: AI’s abundance has zeroed out the value of average work, so competitive edge now hinges on judgment about unprecedented events and unobservable relationships—things models can’t learn. Taste won’t save you; it’s just learned preference. Bet on irreplaceable human context.

podcasts.title: Tribal Dungeons of Global Shipping: AI Agents at Global Scale — Dmitry Buykin, Maersk
podcasts.thesis: The real engineering is converting tribal knowledge into executable procedures—a corpus 20x larger than the agent runtime—not building the agent loop. Accuracy is earned through 100,000+ corrections over nine months, not designed upfront. That's where durable competitive advantage lives.

podcasts.title: Agentic Sites: Building Hyper Personalized Websites — Carlos Sanchez, Adobe
podcasts.thesis: The key insight: hyper-personalized sites are viable not by generating everything, but by constraining AI to swap pre-approved blocks, grounded in brand corpus. This flips the cost equation—making "audience of one" affordable—and proves speed, not frontier models, wins. Investors should watch this as the template for AI-driven marketing i

podcasts.title: Agents Are Where Microservices Were in 2015 — Roberto Milev & Uday Kanagala, Navan
podcasts.thesis: The core insight: agents blur who authorized an action, so Navan treats every tool call as a checkpoint, not the agent itself, routing low-confidence actions to humans. This matters because it redefines accountability in autonomous systems, making them safe enough to deploy in regulated industries like travel.

podcasts.title: THIS is The FASTEST Way to Live Off Compounding. (SHOCKING)
podcasts.thesis: The core insight: compounding’s real power isn’t just growth—it’s the speed of reinvestment, so the fastest path to living off investments is aggressively shortening the reinvestment cycle, not chasing higher returns. This matters because most investors overestimate rate and underestimate time-to-double, delaying financial independence.

podcasts.title: Should American Enterprises Work With Open-Source Chinese Models? | Only 10% of Neo-labs survive
podcasts.thesis: The real cost of AI isn’t the model—it’s the system around it, so cheap open-source models often prove pricier than premium ones once engineering, maintenance, and reliability are factored in. That reframes the Chinese-model debate: security risks matter less than total ownership cost, making US enterprises’ caution economically misguided

podcasts.title: Why New Zealand Is the Only Safe Haven Left
podcasts.thesis: New Zealand’s isolation and low debt make it a haven, but its tiny, trade-dependent economy means it’s a fragile hedge—not a fortress. Investors should see it as a niche diversification play, not a safe harbor, because global shocks still hit it hard.

podcasts.title: Atlassian Chief AI Officer: Building Products for Agents and Humans
podcasts.thesis: Atlassian’s AI chief argues productivity gains fail because tools are built for individuals, not teams. The key insight: design workflows where agents and humans share context and handoffs, making collaboration the unit of value—not solo output. This reframes AI ROI from personal efficiency to systemic team performance.

podcasts.title: Nvidia's Historic Quarter, SaaS Comeback, Bessent vs Druck, America's Debt Crisis, Cancer Vaccine
podcasts.thesis: The core insight: Nvidia’s blowout quarter didn’t just beat earnings—it invalidated the “AI capex bubble” and “SaaSpocalypse” narratives, proving enterprise AI spend is durable, not speculative. This matters because it resets the entire tech investment thesis, rewarding infrastructure owners over software laggards.

podcasts.title: Canada-US Trade Deal Falls Apart
podcasts.thesis: The key insight: Trump’s threat to invoke Section 338—a 50% tariff on all Canadian goods—is a coercive escalation that bypasses USMCA dispute mechanisms, signaling that trade agreements no longer constrain US policy. Investors must price in permanent policy volatility, not a temporary negotiation blip.

podcasts.title: The Bubble’s Final Phase Has Now Begun…
podcasts.thesis: The AI bubble’s final phase is defined by narrative, liquidity, and price momentum—all still strong, so gains can persist even as fundamentals detach. The critical insight: the crash trigger isn’t valuation but a shift in these three forces, making timing the real risk.

podcasts.title: Why Top Founders Are Racing Into AI Infrastructure
podcasts.thesis: The core insight: AI’s bottleneck has shifted from models to physical infrastructure, making capital—not engineering—the primary constraint.
